cards.front: photosynthesis
cards.back: The way green plants make their own food using light, water and carbon dioxide.
cards.say: photosynthesis. The way green plants make their own food using light, water and carbon dioxide.

cards.front: Give the word equation for photosynthesis.
cards.back: Carbon dioxide and water, using light energy, make glucose and oxygen.
cards.say: Give the word equation for photosynthesis.. Carbon dioxide and water, using light energy, make glucose and oxygen.

cards.front: glucose
cards.back: A sugar that plants make in photosynthesis. It is their food.
cards.say: glucose. A sugar that plants make in photosynthesis. It is their food.

cards.front: chlorophyll
cards.back: The green substance in leaves that traps light energy.
cards.say: chlorophyll. The green substance in leaves that traps light energy.

cards.front: chloroplast
cards.back: A tiny green part inside a plant cell where photosynthesis happens.
cards.say: chloroplast. A tiny green part inside a plant cell where photosynthesis happens.

cards.front: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
cards.back: Carbon dioxide.
cards.say: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis? Carbon dioxide.

cards.front: Which gas do plants give out in photosynthesis?
cards.back: Oxygen.
cards.say: Which gas do plants give out in photosynthesis? Oxygen.

cards.front: Where does the water for photosynthesis come from?
cards.back: The roots take it up from the soil.
cards.say: Where does the water for photosynthesis come from? The roots take it up from the soil.

cards.front: stomata
cards.back: Tiny holes, mostly under the leaf, that let gases in and out.
cards.say: stomata. Tiny holes, mostly under the leaf, that let gases in and out.

cards.front: Where does carbon dioxide enter a leaf?
cards.back: Through the stomata, mainly on the underside of the leaf.
cards.say: Where does carbon dioxide enter a leaf? Through the stomata, mainly on the underside of the leaf.

cards.front: Why are leaves usually flat and thin?
cards.back: A large flat surface catches lots of light, and a thin leaf lets gases reach the cells easily.
cards.say: Why are leaves usually flat and thin? A large flat surface catches lots of light, and a thin leaf lets gases reach the cells easily.

cards.front: xylem
cards.back: Tubes in a plant that carry water from the roots up to the leaves.
cards.say: xylem. Tubes in a plant that carry water from the roots up to the leaves.

cards.front: phloem
cards.back: Tubes in a plant that carry sugars made in the leaves to other parts.
cards.say: phloem. Tubes in a plant that carry sugars made in the leaves to other parts.

cards.front: What does a plant do with the glucose it makes?
cards.back: It uses it for energy and to grow, and stores extra as starch.
cards.say: What does a plant do with the glucose it makes? It uses it for energy and to grow, and stores extra as starch.

cards.front: starch
cards.back: A food store in plants, made from glucose. Potatoes and rice contain lots of starch.
cards.say: starch. A food store in plants, made from glucose. Potatoes and rice contain lots of starch.

cards.front: How can you test a leaf for starch?
cards.back: Add iodine solution. It turns blue-black if starch is present.
cards.say: How can you test a leaf for starch? Add iodine solution. It turns blue-black if starch is present.

cards.front: Why does a plant kept in the dark for days make no new starch?
cards.back: Photosynthesis needs light, so with no light no glucose is made.
cards.say: Why does a plant kept in the dark for days make no new starch? Photosynthesis needs light, so with no light no glucose is made.

cards.front: Why does a plant need light?
cards.back: Light is the energy source for photosynthesis.
cards.say: Why does a plant need light? Light is the energy source for photosynthesis.

cards.front: Why does a plant need carbon dioxide?
cards.back: It is one of the raw materials used to make glucose.
cards.say: Why does a plant need carbon dioxide? It is one of the raw materials used to make glucose.

cards.front: How could you show a water plant makes oxygen?
cards.back: Bubbles of gas rise from it in bright light. The gas relights a glowing splint.
cards.say: How could you show a water plant makes oxygen? Bubbles of gas rise from it in bright light. The gas relights a glowing splint.

cards.front: Why are green plants called producers?
cards.back: They make their own food by photosynthesis, and animals depend on that food.
cards.say: Why are green plants called producers? They make their own food by photosynthesis, and animals depend on that food.

cards.front: Why do green plants not grow deep inside a dark cave?
cards.back: There is no light, so they cannot photosynthesise and make food.
cards.say: Why do green plants not grow deep inside a dark cave? There is no light, so they cannot photosynthesise and make food.

cards.front: Why is photosynthesis important for animals?
cards.back: It makes the oxygen they breathe and the food at the start of food chains.
cards.say: Why is photosynthesis important for animals? It makes the oxygen they breathe and the food at the start of food chains.

cards.front: Do plants also respire?
cards.back: Yes. All living things respire. Plants release energy from glucose in all their cells, day and night.
cards.say: Do plants also respire? Yes. All living things respire. Plants release energy from glucose in all their cells, day and night.
